html:
An Apache war leader and medicine man of the Bedonkohe band of the Chiricahua Apache, whose surrender in 1886 ended the long Apache wars against Mexico and the United States.

He was born near the Gila River, in land then claimed by Mexico. In 1858 Mexican soldiers attacked his camp and killed his mother, his wife and his children. He spent years raiding in revenge, and Mexicans gave him the name Geronimo. He was not a chief, but a fierce and trusted fighter and a man said to have spiritual power.

In the 1870s the United States forced the Chiricahua onto the hot, crowded San Carlos reservation in Arizona. Geronimo broke out several times with small bands and raided on both sides of the border. Thousands of soldiers chased a few dozen people, guided by Apache scouts, many of them Western Apache. He finally surrendered to General Nelson Miles in September 1886.

The government then sent all the Chiricahua, including the scouts who had served it, as prisoners of war to Florida and Alabama, where many died, and later to Fort Sill in Oklahoma. Geronimo became a celebrity, sold photographs of himself at fairs, rode in Theodore Roosevelt's inaugural parade in 1905, and dictated his life story. He was never allowed to go home, and died a prisoner at Fort Sill in 1909.
sum: An Apache war leader and medicine man of the Bedonkohe band of the Chiricahua Apache, whose surrender in 1886 ended the long Apache wars against Mexico and the United States.
